name: הוצאת גורם משותף – סכום חזקות v^n + v^(n−1) (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Factorise the following:

\[ {{CT:0}}. \]

[[input:ans]]
[[validation:ans]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: The common factor is the highest common factor (hcf) of the coefficients times every letter that appears in all the terms, each with its lowest power. Divide every term by it, write the quotients in a bracket, and check by expanding.
Step 1 — The common factor
The terms are \({{CT:1}}\) and \({{CT:2}}\). There is no numerical factor (both coefficients are \(1\)). The letter \({{CT:3}}\) appears in both terms, with powers \({{CT:4}}\) and \({{CT:5}}\); the lowest power is \({{CT:5}}\). So the common factor is

\[ {{CT:2}} \]

Step 2 — Dividing each term by the common factor
By the law of exponents \(\dfrac{a^m}{a^n}=a^{m-n}\):

\[ \frac{{{CT:1}}}{{{CT:2}}}={{CT:3}}^{{{CT:4}}-{{CT:5}}}={{CT:3}},\qquad \frac{{{CT:2}}}{{{CT:2}}}=1 \]

The important thing is to remember the \(1\): the term \({{CT:2}}\) does not disappear, it leaves \(1\) in the bracket.
Step 3 — The factorised form
Check by expanding the brackets:

\[ {{CT:2}}\cdot {{CT:3}}+{{CT:2}}\cdot 1={{CT:0}} \]

So the factorised form is

\[ {{CT:0}}={{CT:6}}. \]

on_true.feedback: Remember when factorising \({{CT:0}} = {{CT:6}}\) and not equal to \({{CT:2}}({{CT:3}}+0) = {{CT:1}} \)
